correct_answer: perfectly elastic, so that the total kinetic energy of the colliding molecules is conserved
explanation: Kinetic theory assumes that a gas molecule suffers no loss of kinetic energy in a collision. Momentum and kinetic energy are both conserved. This is why a gas kept at constant temperature in an insulated vessel maintains a steady pressure indefinitely; if any energy were lost per collision the pressure would keep decreasing.

correct_answer: a molecule spends almost all of its time in free straight line motion
explanation: If each collision lasts for a vanishingly small time, then almost the entire lifetime of a molecule is spent travelling freely in a straight line. This is what makes it meaningful to define a free path and a mean free path, and it also justifies calculating pressure as a sequence of instantaneous momentum transfers. The frequency of collisions can still be very large; a short duration does not mean a small number.

correct_answer: zero and a non zero positive quantity
explanation: Molecular motion is completely random, so for every molecule moving with a certain velocity there is on average another moving with the opposite velocity. The vector sum, and hence the average velocity, is zero for a container at rest. The square of a speed is always positive, so no cancellation is possible and the mean square speed is a definite positive number. That is exactly why pressure is written using the mean square speed and not the average velocity.

At low pressure the molecules are far apart, so their own volume is a negligible fraction of the vessel and the attractive forces are weak. At high temperature the average kinetic energy is large compared with the potential energy of attraction, so the attractive forces hardly affect the motion. Both requirements of the ideal gas model are therefore best satisfied at low pressure and high temperature.

correct_answer: along a straight line with constant velocity
explanation: Kinetic theory neglects intermolecular forces except during the brief collision. With zero net force the acceleration is zero, so the molecule travels in a straight line at constant speed. The straight segment between two collisions is exactly what is called a free path, and its average value is the mean free path.

correct_answer: the capacitance and the stored charge both rise K times while the field between the plates is unchanged
explanation: The battery holds the potential difference V constant. The capacitance becomes K C₀, so the charge Q = C V becomes K times larger, drawn from the battery. The field between the plates is E = V / d, and since neither V nor d changes, the field is unchanged.

Capacitance is the charge stored per unit rise of potential, C = Q / V, so the unit is coulomb per volt. This unit is named the farad. One farad is a very large capacitance, so practical capacitors are rated in microfarad or picofarad.

The equivalent capacitance is 2 × 3 / (2 + 3) = 1.2 microF, so the common charge is Q = 1.2 × 10⁻⁶ x 100 = 1.2 × 10⁻⁴ C. Then the potential difference across the 2 microF capacitor is 1.2 × 10⁻⁴ / (2 × 10⁻⁶) = 60 V and across the 3 microF capacitor it is 1.2 × 10⁻⁴ / (3 × 10⁻⁶) = 40 V. These add to 100 V, as they must.

correct_answer: the charge is the same on each capacitor in a series arrangement, while the potential difference is the same across each in a parallel arrangement
explanation: In a series chain the inner plates are isolated, so induction gives every capacitor the same charge while the applied voltage divides between them. In a parallel arrangement all the capacitors are connected across the same two nodes, so they share the same potential difference while the charge divides in proportion to the capacitances.

Let the initial energy be U. With the battery connected the voltage is fixed and the capacitance doubles, so the energy becomes 2 U, the extra energy coming from the battery. With the battery disconnected the charge is fixed and the capacitance doubles, so the energy becomes U / 2, the difference being spent in drawing the slab in. The ratio is 2 U to U / 2, that is 4 : 1.

The parallel pair gives 6 + 6 = 12 microF. Combining this in series with 6 microF gives 1 / C = 1 / 12 + 1 / 6 = 1 / 12 + 2 / 12 = 3 / 12, so C = 4 microF, which is less than the smallest capacitance in the series part of the network.

In the metal the free electrons keep moving until the induced surface charges create a field that exactly cancels the applied field, so the internal field is zero. In the dielectric the charges are bound and can only be displaced slightly, so the bound surface charges produce a partial opposing field and the net field is reduced to E / K, here E / 4. A conductor can be regarded as the limiting case of a dielectric with an infinitely large dielectric constant.

Free electrons in the metal move under the applied field and pile up on the surfaces. Their own field opposes the applied field, and the movement continues until the two cancel exactly. correct_answer: to reduce the ripple by charging at the peaks and discharging slowly through the load
explanation: During each pulse the capacitor charges to nearly the peak value. When the pulse falls away the diode stops conducting and the capacitor supplies the load, so the output voltage sags only a little before the next pulse arrives. The result is a much smaller ripple riding on a higher average voltage.

correct_answer: two diodes in opposite arms conduct while the other two are reverse biased
explanation: The four diodes form a ring. In one half cycle the two diodes whose arrows point away from the positive terminal and towards the load are forward biased, while the other two are reverse biased. When the input reverses, the roles swap. In both cases the current traverses the load in the same direction, giving full wave rectification without a centre tap.

Both halves of the input cycle are used and each produces a pulse of the same polarity through the load. Two pulses per input cycle means the output repeats twice as often, giving 2 × 50 = 100 Hz. This is one reason a full wave output is easier to smooth than a half wave output.

A half wave circuit uses a single diode which conducts during one half cycle only. A bridge circuit uses four diodes arranged so that two opposite arms conduct during each half cycle, which routes current through the load in the same direction both times. The centre tap version of the full wave circuit uses two diodes and a centre tapped transformer.

correct_answer: works without any external bias and delivers electrical power to the load
explanation: Both devices generate carriers when light falls on the junction, but their purposes differ. A photodiode is reverse biased and is used to measure light, so it draws power from the supply. A solar cell has no external supply, has a large junction area to collect as much light as possible, and its photo generated carriers drive a current through the external load, so it supplies power.

Forward bias injects electrons into the p-region and holes into the n-region. When an injected electron recombines with a hole, the energy released is close to the band gap energy and in suitable materials it appears as a photon. Since injection happens only in forward bias, an LED must be forward biased to glow.
Substituting, Eg = 1240 / 620 = 2.0 eV. Materials with a gap near 2 eV therefore emit red light. A larger gap gives shorter wavelengths, which is why blue LEDs need materials with gaps near 3 eV.

correct_answer: occurs in heavily doped junctions at low reverse voltages by direct field ionisation of covalent bonds
explanation: In a heavily doped junction the depletion layer is very thin, so a reverse voltage of only a few volt produces an enormous field that tears electrons directly out of covalent bonds. That is Zener breakdown. In a lightly doped junction the layer is wide, the field is smaller, and breakdown occurs only at a higher voltage when carriers gain enough kinetic energy between collisions to create new pairs. That is avalanche breakdown.
A regulating Zener maintains approximately its breakdown voltage across the load.
In reverse breakdown the Zener voltage remains nearly constant over a useful current range.
The resistor drops excess voltage and keeps the Zener current within its safe range.

correct_answer: increases markedly, because many more minority carriers are generated thermally
explanation: The reverse current is limited by how fast minority carriers are produced, not by the voltage. Heating breaks many more covalent bonds, so minority carriers appear at a much greater rate on both sides of the junction. Every one that reaches the depletion layer is swept across, so the reverse current rises sharply. In silicon it roughly doubles for each 10° Celsius rise.

First the field: E = 0.7 / (0.5 × 10⁻⁶) = 1.4 × 10⁶ V/m. Then the force: F = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ x 1.4 × 10⁶ = 2.24 × 10⁻¹³ N. Although the number looks tiny, it is enormous compared with the force on an electron in an ordinary conductor, which is why carriers are swept across the layer almost instantly.

correct_answer: equal in magnitude and opposite in direction, so that the net current is zero
explanation: Diffusion drives majority carriers across the junction, which builds up the space charge and the barrier field. That field drives minority carriers the other way as a drift current. The barrier grows until the two currents are exactly equal and opposite, so the net current through an isolated junction is zero.

correct_answer: Majority carriers diffusing down their concentration gradients
explanation: There are many holes on the p-side and very few on the n-side, and many electrons on the n-side and very few on the p-side. These concentration differences drive holes to the right and electrons to the left, and both flows constitute the diffusion current, which is therefore a majority carrier current.

Making the p side positive applies a potential difference that opposes the built in barrier, so the two subtract. The effective barrier is 0.7 - 0.3 = 0.4 V. The remaining barrier is still large enough to keep the forward current small, which is why a silicon diode begins to conduct appreciably only near 0.7 V.
